title: Backwards sequential focus navigation can get trapped if starting point is inside focused element
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

If the [sequential focus navigation starting point](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#sequential-focus-navigation-starting-point) is set inside the focused element, but before any focusable descendants, then backwards sequential focus navigation will not change the focused element. See https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=316027 for example — Blink and Gecko don't currently have this issue since they don't implement [step 2 here](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#sequential-focus-navigation:sequential-focus-navigation-starting-point-2) according to the spec (they instead use the starting point only if there is no focused element). This could be solved by

1. explicitly checking whether sequential focus navigation ended up returning the currently focused element, and continuing on if so, or
2. changing [step 7 here](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#sequential-focus-navigation:sequential-focus-navigation-starting-point-4) to "Set the sequential focus navigation starting point to *candidate*" (so that the first shift+tab in this case doesn't change the focused element, but pressing shift+tab does)

(or maybe there is some other option I haven't considered…)

Option 2 is quite unintuitive if a focus ring is displayed when a keyboard-focusable element is click-focused (this currently happens on WebKit and Gecko, and only if the shift key is pressed on Blink), because then the focus ring would not move when shift+tab is pressed. But if the focus ring only appears after keyboard focus navigation, then it's probably alright.
